feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — A coordinate system is an abstract mathematical structure, not a tangible object.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — It is a human-invented conceptual framework.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not inspired by or derived from biology.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — It does not depend on energy to exist as a concept.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Only observable through representation, not inherently.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Abstract, not tied to material substance.
feedback.Active: Excluded — It does not perform operations by itself.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Excluded — While invented, it is not a functional artifact per se.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — It represents spatial logic but does not emit effects.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Used in logic but does not process on its own.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Interaction happens via tools that use it, not the concept itself.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Can be applied in systems, but not inherently part of one.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Not essential to any single system.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Coordinate systems use symbolic notation to represent space.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Encodes spatial meaning and structure.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Defined by mathematical rules and conventions.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Composed of axes, origins, and units in structured hierarchy.
feedback.Normative: Included — Used to define expected spatial behavior or organization.
feedback.Meta: Included — Often used to define the structure of systems that define things.
feedback.Temporal: Included — May be extended to include time (e.g., spacetime coordinates).
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Exists and functions as a virtual mathematical abstraction.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists because of shared mathematical conventions.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Defined and taught by academic and scientific institutions.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not tied to any person or role.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Standardized in technical fields and disciplines.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Fundamental to navigation, GIS, CAD, and many industries.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Coordinate systems have historically been linked to geopolitical and cartographic disputes.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Appears in standardized exams, curricula, and scientific practice.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Impacts justice in areas like urban planning, surveillance, and geospatial equity.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the coordinate system as a fully abstract, symbolic, rule-based structure with institutional and ethical implications. Its meaning and application depend on convention and social adoption, rather than any intrinsic functionality.
